newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: DOOHAN AIMS FOR FOURTH GRAND PRIX WIN IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: DOOHAN AIMS FOR FOURTH GRAND PRIX WIN IN 1997.

text.p: Three times world 500cc champion Michael Doohan will be gunning for his fourth straight title at the 1997 motorcycling Grand Prix opening in Malaysia on Friday.
The 31-year-old Australian, riding a Honda, is the hottest bet for Sunday's race at the Shah Alam circuit.
Doohan is used to the tight and twisty 3.505 km am track, where he won three races.
His biggest challenge is expected to come from Italian Luca Cadalora, another Honda rider, and Suzuki rider and fellow Australian Daryll Beattie.
Cadalora, a two times 250cc champion, won the 500cc race in Malaysia last year but could not sustain the pace for the rest of the season and dropped to third in the standings in 1996.
Beattie, who ended 1996 with head and wrist injuries, is also promising a stormy return with a brand new Suzuki XR87 motorcycle.

Suzuki team officials say the 26-year-old Australian has completely recovered while his motorcycle itself has been revised in chassis and geometry and reinforced with better suspension and mid-range power.
Others to look out for in the 500cc race are Spain's Alex Criville and Brazil's Alex Barros, both Honda riders, and Japan's Norifumi Abe, who will be astride a Yamaha.
